title: Kitchen and Postcard
premise: Marguerite Crane's struggling café joins a town charity pen-pal program to drum up goodwill, and she's matched with an anonymous correspondent who turns out to be Theo Vance, the bank officer handling her loan and the man she blames for her late brother's debts. Their letters, written without names, strip away old grudges until the truth of their identities threatens everything they've built on paper. When Marguerite discovers who he is mid-correspondence, she must choose between protecting her pride and trusting the man behind the words. On the last ferry of the season, Theo chooses her over his transfer, and together they save the café as a community venture — choosing love against duty.
about_author: Rafael Eastwick is a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, harbors, and small towns where everyone knows your order. He lives on a coastal island with his partner and a temperamental espresso machine.

chapters.title: Flour, Ink, and Bad Odds
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Facing a third missed payment, she signs her café up for the town's anonymous pen-pal fundraiser and vents her frustrations into her first letter to 'a stranger.' Meanwhile, bank officer Theo Vance, reviewing her file, receives her letter by clerical error instead of his assigned match. The beat: weary defiance meeting quiet curiosity.

chapters.title: Letters Without Names
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo, recognizing her handwriting but not revealing himself, answers anyway; their correspondence deepens as both confess fears they'd never say aloud. In person at the café, they spar bitterly, each unaware the other is the tender voice on paper. The beat: dramatic irony tightening — intimacy growing in one world, hostility in the other.

chapters.title: The Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A dropped envelope reveals Theo as her correspondent the same week he delivers her final foreclosure warning. Feeling betrayed twice over, she burns his letters publicly at the harbor festival, wounding him before witnesses. The beat: climax of heartbreak — pride weaponized, duty and love colliding head-on.

chapters.title: Last Ferry Out
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, closing on both. Instead of boarding his transfer ferry, Theo reads his final letter aloud at the dock, owning every word and his part in her brother's story. Marguerite arrives as the gangway rises; the town rallies behind them, converting the café into a co-op. The beat: resolution — the whole heart risked, kept.
